title: Mass-summable series of currents in ℝ^P: the sum is a current with mass and support bounds, and is integer multiplicity if the terms are (Simon 3.13)
statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, d := k + 1, and let X_i ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) (i ∈ ℕ) with Σ_i M(X_i) < ∞ (sum in [0, ∞], M = mass = M_{ℝ^P}). Then there is Y ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with the following properties: for every ω ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P) the real series Σ_i X_i(ω) converges to Y(ω) (HasSum); M(Y) ≤ Σ_i M(X_i); spt Y ⊆ closure(⋃_i spt X_i); and if every X_i is integer multiplicity, then so is Y.
lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (X : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (k + 1)), ∑' i, (X i).mass < ∞ → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (k + 1), (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (k + 1), HasSum (fun i => X i ω) (Y ω)) ∧ Y.mass ≤ ∑' i, (X i).mass ∧ Y.support ⊆ closure (⋃ i, (X i).support) ∧ ((∀ i, IsIntegerMultiplicity (X i)) → IsIntegerMultiplicity Y)
